issues.title: In-place finalize: combine radix partitions without re-materializing first-seen groups
issues.hypothesis: The q18 subquery HASH_GROUP_BY (4.6-5.0s CPU, ~95% of the query) is bound by a fixed cost per group, not per input row. SQL experiments on the current build: orders GROUP BY o_orderkey (15M rows, 15M groups) takes 5.43s CPU, while lineitem GROUP BY l_orderkey (60M rows, 15M groups) takes 5.0s. 1.5M groups takes 0.48s, so ~320ns/group whatever the size, which means it is not about cache size. Removing the aggregate drops it to 3.17s and count(*) gives 4.29s, so the cost grows with row width. That points at row materialization and copying, not at probing (E0001 cut probes 4x and gained only ~1-3% wall). With 8 threads, every surviving group is materialized twice. Once in the sink (thread-local HT abandoned into partitioned TupleData). Then again in RadixHTLocalSourceState::Finalize, which calls ht->Combine(*partition.data): FlushMoveState scans and gathers the groups, FindOrCreateGroups appends a brand-new row (scatter plus InitializeStates) for every group first seen in the partition, then CombineStates. Later Scan gathers it again. For high-cardinality aggregates most groups are first-seen in finalize, so the second append, init and combine is pure copying. An in-place finalize would build only a pointer table over the existing partition rows. A first-seen row is used as the target directly, with no copy. A duplicate row gets its states combined into the target and is dropped. The scan then gathers from the list of live row pointers.
issues.plan: 1) In src/execution/aggregate_hashtable.cpp (and its header), add GroupedAggregateHashTable::CombineInPlace(TupleDataCollection &data, vector<data_ptr_t> &live_rows). Scan `data` with TupleDataPinProperties::KEEP_EVERYTHING_PINNED, gathering the group columns and the hash as FlushMoveState does. Probe the ht_entry_t table using the same salt and linear-probing logic as FindOrCreateGroupsInternal. When a slot is empty, store the source row pointer itself with entry.SetPointer(source_row) and push it to live_rows; do not append. When the salt matches, compare with row_matcher.Match against the pointed-to rows. On a match, call RowOperations::CombineStates(source -> target). Simplest path: factor the probe loop so it returns an 'is new' selection plus target addresses without appending. 2) In src/execution/radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp, in RadixHTLocalSourceState::Finalize, use CombineInPlace only when !sink.external, !layout.HasDestructor() and sink.scan_pin_properties == DESTROY_AFTER_DONE (no multi-scan). Keep partition.data alive and pinned, and store live_rows in the AggregatePartition. Otherwise use the existing path. 3) In RadixHTLocalSourceState::Scan, when the partition has live_rows, take slices of up to STANDARD_VECTOR_SIZE pointers into a row_locations Vector. Use data_collection.Gather(row_locations, sel, count, column_ids, scan_chunk, ...) for the group columns, then the existing FinalizeStates on those addresses. Reset the collection at the end. The HT pointer table can be freed right after finalize. Size the pointer table with GetCapacityForCount(partition.data->Count()), as is done today.
issues.expected_gain: q18: the subquery aggregate drops one full row materialization (scatter, init, combine and the extra blocks) for ~all 15M groups. Estimate 15-25% of aggregate CPU, so roughly -10..-20% on q18 wall.
issues.generality: Any multi-threaded hash aggregate with many groups, where groups mostly survive the thread-local HT uniquely: high-cardinality GROUP BY, DISTINCT, and the sub-aggregates in TPC-H q18/q10/q13-like shapes and in dedup queries. Low-cardinality aggregates have tiny partitions, so they see no change. Possible slowdowns: the scan gathers through random pointers instead of sequentially, so scan locality is a little worse. Pinning the whole partition while finalizing is the same as today's KEEP pin during combine.
issues.risk: Medium. Correctness rests on (a) never destroying states of rows that are still live (restricted to layouts without destructors), (b) heap pointers for VARCHAR keys staying valid (KEEP_EVERYTHING_PINNED, non-external only), (c) multi-scan and external paths falling back. The bench verifies results on hidden shapes, so the fallback gates must be conservative.

issues.title: Instrument and fix radix sink partition growth / repartition copies for high-cardinality aggregates
issues.hypothesis: Group materialization costs ~320ns/group, and the cost grows with row width (no-agg 3.17s, count 4.29s, sum 5.43s CPU for 15M groups), which suggests repeated whole-row copies. RadixHTConfig::SetRadixBits is capped by ExternalRadixBits(true), which uses temporary_memory_state->GetReservation(). The initial reservation is only num_threads*ht_size, a few tens of MB, which may keep sink radix bits at InitialSinkRadixBits (3) or force repeated Repartition() copies of all thread-local data as bits grow by REPARTITION_RADIX_BITS, as MaybeRepartition shows. This is unverified: the first step is to log (debug only) final radix bits and the repartition count per thread on q18.
issues.plan: First measure: temporary counters in MaybeRepartition (radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp) for repartition events and bytes moved. If repartitions move a large share of the data, start the sink at the maximum sink radix bits when the HLL/ADAPTIVITY decision shows high cardinality (in DecideAdaptation), so the data is partitioned once.
issues.risk: Low-medium; memory-reservation interplay with external aggregation.

output.memory:
## Memory (planner, q18 specialisation run)

### Workload facts (q18 only visible template; baseline ~610-625 ms hot, 8 threads)
- Plan: IN-subquery `GROUP BY l_orderkey HAVING sum(l_quantity) > X` over all of lineitem (60M rows -> 15M groups -> ~111 after HAVING).
  Its HASH_GROUP_BY = 4.6-5.0s CPU (~95% of operator time). Rest small: outer lineitem scan 0.17s, join probe 0.25s,
  orders scan 0.18s, SEMI join 0.10s, customer scan 0.16s, join 0.3-0.4s.
- The group key arrives compressed as UINTEGER (__internal_compress_integral projection), fixed-width. sum_no_overflow(decimal).
- lineitem is clustered on the key (~4 equal keys per run).

### Key measurements (R2, via dbe-tool sql EXPLAIN ANALYZE; SET threads=1 works inside sql)
- Aggregate cost is PER GROUP (~320ns CPU/group), NOT per row and NOT about cache size:
  orders GROUP BY o_orderkey 15M rows/15M groups 5.43s; lineitem 60M rows/15M groups 5.0s; 1.5M groups 0.48s;
  60M groups 14.5s. Single thread (grow strategy, no finalize combine) 5.24s, about the same CPU.
- Grows with row width: no aggregate 3.17s, count(*) 4.29s, sum(int) 5.43s (15M groups). => copying/materializing rows dominates.
- E0001 (run-collapse, fewer probes) cut HT CPU 13% but wall only 1-3%: probing isn't the bottleneck.

### Codebase facts
- Radix sink: Sink() -> ht.AddChunk (aggregate_hashtable.cpp:519) -> TryAddCompressedGroups -> Hash -> FindOrCreateGroupsInternal (:641).
  Thread-local HT capacity starts at 32768 (8 threads), Abandon() when full; data goes into PartitionedTupleData.
- DecideAdaptation (radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp:424): SkipLookups if HLL unique >95%; ADAPTIVITY_THRESHOLD 1M rows.
- MaybeRepartition (:479) grows radix bits, capped by ExternalRadixBits(true), which depends on temporary-memory reservation.
- Source: RadixHTLocalSourceState::Finalize (:853) builds a new HT per partition and calls ht->Combine(TupleDataCollection)
  (aggregate_hashtable.cpp:883: FlushMoveState scan+gather, FindOrCreateGroups appends new rows, CombineStates).
  Scan (:910) scans partition.data, then FinalizeStates. So each group gets materialized twice + gathered twice.
- RowOperations Initialize/Combine/Finalize/UpdateStates (row_aggregate.cpp) are vectorized via function pointers; cheap.
- profile.md plan is truncated; `dbe-tool profile q18.m0` prints the full plan (the tool blocks pipes like grep -v).

### Directions
- R1 (E0001 run-collapse): retired, noise. Good implementation of a wrong target.
- R2 dispatched: in-place finalize (pointer-table combine over existing partition rows, scan via live-row pointers;
  gated to non-external, no destructors, no multi-scan). If it fails, check whether the cost is in the sink instead (next issue).
- Backlog: instrument repartition copies / radix bits in sink (filed). Not filed yet:
  * a bloom/hash filter from the 111-key join build into the outer lineitem scan (only ~0.4s CPU, small upside);
  * perfect/direct-index HA on a dense int key: the key range is ~4x the group count (sparse keys), so 2^26 per-thread tables are too much memory;
    it would need key-range-striped ownership. User auto-memory: 22-bit perfect HA worked on q13 in another run.
